chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Fadl al-Nahwi, from Abu Ja'far al-Ahwal Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "If you have prayed four rak'at of the night prayer before the dawn breaks, complete the prayer whether it rises or not." And it is preferable to defer completing the night prayer to the dawn prayer, then complete it after finishing the dawn prayer. What indicates this is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: How should one complete the night prayer if dawn breaks before finishing it?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that completing the four rak'at of night prayer before dawn is valid whether or not the sun has risen, yet he recommends prioritizing the obligatory dawn prayer first. This preference highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing voluntary night worship with the timely fulfillment of obligatory duties, ensuring the dawn prayer is not neglected due to the completion of the night prayer.
